proposed_topic_definitions.PROPOSED:TRIVIAL-VS-VACUOUS-TRUTH: A source calls an implication 'vacuously true' where it is in fact trivially true through its consequent (or a tautology), or the reverse (first needed by this record).

statement: S2131 argues that forcing a static layer invariant P into the schema 𝓘(P): ∀K,o. Admissible(o,K) ⇒ (P(K) ⇒ P(δ(K,o))) makes it 'vacuously true, because the antecedent never engages them'. Read with standard logic, if P does not depend on K the inner implication is P ⇒ P, a tautology, so 𝓘(P) holds trivially whatever Admissible is. This is trivial truth through the consequent, not vacuous truth through a false antecedent (Admissible may hold). In transition-system theory a state-independent property is a degenerate case of an inductive invariant (preserved by every transition), not a type error. On this reading the defect is that the schema cannot distinguish substantive layer invariants from tautologies, which is weaker than 'category error'. The researcher's comparison uses outside knowledge and does not claim the source intended it.
